candidate_findings.message: No written North Star exists; write it with the user before this unit is judged. Findings measured against the PR's own claims instead.

Stream lifecycle (caller owns/disposes stream, seeking requires seekable stream, non-seekable limits) is claimed in the PR but absent from XML docs on StreamMediaSource, FromStream and the Stream property.
Tizen only throws when Stream is not null; a StreamMediaSource with null Stream silently does nothing, contrary to 'explicitly unsupported'. Message says 'not yet supported', implying future support.
PR describes StreamExtensions.windows.cs returning application/octet-stream; diff ships a shared magic-byte sniffer (listed as Future). Android file name also differs from description.
Sample is registered and present, but it is unverified whether it demonstrates stream lifetime ownership or Tizen behaviour, both key for secure-app consumers.

Implicit operator is Stream -> StreamMediaSource? on the subclass; C# does not consider operators on subclasses of the target, so the advertised `MediaSource source = myStream;` fails with CS0029. Add `implicit operator MediaSource(Stream)` on MediaSource plus a test.

(int)RequestedLength allocates the full range in one buffer (overflow >2GB); a single Read may be short yet request is finished; exceptions swallowed and FinishLoading() still called instead of FinishLoadingWithError.
Non-seekable streams report ContentLength = 0 (empty resource) and are read from current position; likely cannot play on iOS at all, worse than 'limited functionality'.

StreamDataSourceFactory Java peer disposed before the player's ProgressiveMediaSource that holds it is replaced (also 804-808; same pattern on macios:296 for the loader); loader-thread call into disposed peer can crash.
UpdateSourceStream disposes the MemoryStream the player is still reading before assigning the new source; OnDisappearing (44-52) disposes it without clearing Source.
GetStreamContentType duplicates sniffing instead of reusing shared GetMimeType, maps all non-qt input (incl. audio) to public.mpeg-4, and resets Position in finally without IO/NotSupported guards.
Doc comment says 'on Windows platform' but file is shared; single 0x47 byte check (line 142) classifies any stream starting with 'G' as video/mp2t.
FromStream returns StreamMediaSource unlike sibling factories returning MediaSource, and lacks ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(stream) required by the codestyle guideline this diff adds.

Stream branch sets Player.Source instead of Player.MediaPlayer.Set*Source like other branches; non-seekable streams likely throw from AsRandomAccessStream; created WinMediaSource never disposed on source change.
Open throws InvalidOperationException where ExoPlayer expects IOException, so it is treated as an unexpected error rather than a source error.

Undescribed out-of-scope behaviour changes: File.Open(FileMode.Create)->File.OpenRead fix, HttpClient static->instance (line 32); also unrelated codestyle, LazyViewTests, PopupsPage, Info.plist edits; PR file list wrong.

Delete the magic-byte sniffer: contradicts the PR (octet-stream default, sniffing listed as Future), shared file only Windows calls. Use the default MIME type at MediaManager.windows.cs:344; saves ~160 lines.
Tests exercise only the sniffer; delete with it, saving 283 lines.
Revert formatting churn expanding one-line listener stubs into 4-line bodies; unrelated to streams, ~100 lines of diff noise.
Revert member reordering in File/Uri/ResourceMediaSource; unrelated refactor, plus a stray double blank line.
Unrelated style-rule addition; the end-of-file change drops a closing code fence, likely accidental (rigor counted fences and says they are now balanced).
Whitespace-only unrelated change; revert.
Unrelated test edit (Task.Delay -> polling loop); move out of this PR.
HttpClient static->instance and File.Open->File.OpenRead (line 617) are undisclosed non-stream behaviour changes; revert or call out.
Factory dispose-and-null repeated three times in PlatformUpdateSource and again in CreateMediaItemFromStream; restating comments; ~8 lines removable.
Empty view model is a BasePage<T> repo convention; keep as is (no change).
Title="MediaElement" duplicates the existing page's title; rename to indicate 'from Stream'.

Sample copies the full speed/volume/mute/slider surface from the existing page; only in-memory copy, Open Video and Record Video are stream-specific; ~100 lines removable. Downloading Big Buck Bunny into memory is heavy.
`MediaSource source = myStream;` and `mediaElement.Source = stream;` will not compile (CS0029): the operator lives on the subclass; no test exercises it.
Exceptions swallowed by Debug.WriteLine, then FinishLoading() (line 35) reports success with no data; never FinishLoadingWithError, so MediaFailed gets no cause.
Single Stream.Read may be short yet request is finished (silent truncation); (int)RequestedLength allocates entire to-end range, overflows >2GB.
Non-seekable streams report ContentLength=0 and ignore RequestedOffset, returning wrong bytes silently; cannot play on Apple platforms.
'Works with audio and video' unsupported: GetStreamContentType only returns public.mpeg-4 or quicktime, so MP3/WAV/FLAC are mislabelled; shared sniffer never reaches Apple.
AsRandomAccessStream throws NotSupportedException for non-seekable streams inside an async ValueTask that MapSource does not await; exception unobserved, MediaFailed never fires.

Vacuous test: FromStream is statically typed StreamMediaSource, so BeAssignableTo holds for any non-null return; doesn't assert .Stream == stream. No tests for converter, operators, or platform pipelines.
Sample disposes the stream the player is still reading (also OnDisappearing 44-52), violating the PR's own caller-owns-lifetime guidance.

All StreamDataSource instances share one Stream/Position (races on loader thread); Open throws non-IOException types; after Stop/Play re-prepare a non-seekable stream is already consumed and ends silently.
Previous factory (Android, also 804-808) / resource loader (macios 227, 296) disposed while player still holds old source; in-flight callbacks hit disposed peer.
Throws synchronously from mapper after Unprepare and CurrentStateChanged(Opening), leaving element stuck in Opening rather than MediaFailed.
PR text mismatches code: Windows already sniffs magic bytes (not octet-stream default), file is shared not .windows.cs, Android/macOS file paths differ.
Unmentioned behaviour changes: HttpClient static->instance and File.Open(Create)->OpenRead (586, 617); both real fixes but deserve their own mention/commit.
Out-of-scope edits slipped in: codestyle section, PopupsPage whitespace, MediaSource member reordering, Android listener reformatting (812-928), LazyViewTests flaky-test fix.
FromStream returns StreamMediaSource unlike FromFile/FromUri, breaking the 'follows existing patterns' claim and making the FromStream test unable to fail.
`MediaSource source = myStream;` fails CS0029; add `implicit operator MediaSource(Stream stream) => FromStream(stream);` to MediaSource.shared.cs and a compiling test.

FillDataRequest: int overflow / whole-file allocation for to-end requests, short reads answered as complete, errors swallowed then FinishLoading(); loop in chunks with long math, honor RequestsAllDataToEndOfResource, FinishLoadingWithError on failure.
Non-seekable or disposed stream makes AsRandomAccessStream throw out of PlatformUpdateSource instead of raising MediaFailed; buffer or fail via MediaFailed inside try/catch.

Open/Read throw managed exceptions (InvalidOperation, ArgumentOutOfRange, ObjectDisposed) across JNI instead of IOException/DataSourceException, risking crash instead of OnPlayerError; non-seekable reopen at 0 silently continues mid-stream.

Factory disposed before media source replaced (also 804-808), with SetPlayerData awaited in between; later CreateDataSource on disposed peer throws 'Unable to activate instance' (no JNI handle ctor). Drop reference or dispose after replacement.

Only QuickTime vs MPEG-4 distinguished; MP3/WAV/M4A/ADTS declared public.mpeg-4; duplicates shared sniffer; Read/Position exceptions escape; trailing literal should use DefaultContentType. Map GetMimeType to UTType.

Sample disposes stream before swapping Source and in OnDisappearing while still bound; semaphore ineffective since null check and assignment happen outside it. Clear Source first, hold lock across swap.

StreamMediaSource with null Stream returns stale mediaItem builder and keeps old factory, so old stream replays; same on macios 225-229. Clear factory and return null; guard FromStream with ThrowIfNull.
Any stream starting with 0x47 reported as video/mp2t (false positive); also require sync byte at offset 188. Class summary wrongly says Windows-only.

Only test is FromStream type check; implicit operators (would have caught CS0029), ToString, SourceChanged, converter, Android range logic and macOS loader untested; GetMimeType_DoesNotRewindWhenAtZero misnamed.
Throw happens after CurrentStateChanged(Opening), so state sticks at Opening and exception escapes the mapper; log + MediaFailed + return, or throw before the state change.

The hasRepoScript fallback in handleGitUpdate cannot fire for global installs: classifyInstallPath returns npm-global/pnpm-global for any /node_modules/ path, so those never reach it. It only fires for source checkouts, where it offers `npm install -g @aoagents/ao@latest`. That leaves the checkout un-updated and installs a second global copy that may shadow the npm-linked ao. A rebuild hint is the correct action.
The 'script unavailable' fallback test mocks detectInstallMethod as 'git', so it locks in the source-checkout → npm install -g behaviour rather than testing the global-install scenario from #1252.

The default REPO_ROOT ($(dirname BASH_SOURCE)/..) now resolves to .../assets after the move. Run directly without AO_REPO_ROOT, the root is wrong and layout detection can never pick package-install (same in ao-update.sh line 43).
The 'bundled doctor script is available' check is self-referential and always passes in practice.
The regex-escape pattern /[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g is malformed and escapes nothing. The test passes only because an unescaped '.' acts as a wildcard.

The fallback only runs when the install is classified 'git', never for the global npm/pnpm installs of #1252. Where it does fire, it offers npm install -g and reports 'Update complete', replacing the earlier clear 'Script not found' error with a misleading action that never updates the checkout.
The test forces detectInstallMethod=git with hasRepoScript=false. It locks in the questionable fallback and never exercises a real global-install path, though its name suggests #1252 coverage.

Dropping the scripts/ao-update.sh guard means any non-node_modules location with .git four levels up counts as 'git' (e.g. vendored inside another repo). The 'unknown' test was deleted with no replacement guard.
The fix relies on CLI_DIST_ROOT resolving to dist/ in a packaged install, but no test checks it. hasRepoScript is mocked in every caller test.
Script cwd silently changed from the repo root to process.cwd(). ao-doctor.sh walks up from $PWD to find config, so git installs now find config from the user's directory.
The REPO_ROOT fallback resolves to src/assets after the move (same in ao-update.sh line 43). Direct invocation without AO_REPO_ROOT uses the wrong root, and the update script's smoke-test paths fail.
The packaged-install test sets AO_SCRIPT_LAYOUT explicitly, so the script's own layout detection goes untested. The fake dist/index.js makes the runtime sanity check pass regardless.
The 'bundled doctor script is available' check is self-referential and can only pass in normal use.

The escape regex closes its character class early and never escapes anything. A checkout path containing +, ( or [ would break the test; use /[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g correctly as /[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g → /[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/ fixed to /[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g with the class written [.*+?^${}()|[\]\\].

When detection says git but ao-update.sh is missing, this branch hard-codes the npm-global command and can install a global copy that shadows the npm link launcher. It is nearly unreachable; a rebuild hint would be more accurate.
Install detection returns 'git' whenever .git exists four levels up, with no second signal. Checking for packages/cli/package.json under that root would restore one.
The REPO_ROOT fallback was not updated after the move and resolves to .../assets (same in ao-update.sh line 43). Direct runs fall into the source-checkout branch and fail its checks.
hasRepoScript now checks bundled assets, not repo scripts. hasBundledScript would fit.
The scripts' cwd changed from the repo root to the caller's cwd. ao-update.sh cd's itself, but the doctor now searches for config from the user's cwd, an undocumented behaviour change.

AO_SCRIPT_LAYOUT is passed from TS while ao-doctor.sh also re-derives the layout by sniffing files: two detection mechanisms for one fact. resolveScriptLayout's override branch exists only for the env var.
resolveScriptLayoutFromPath and resolveDefaultRepoRootFromPath are exported only for tests and are '/node_modules/' substring heuristics.
The error message repeats the scripts directory inside 'Expected at' and in the parenthetical. Dropping the parenthetical also removes the test's regex escaping.

The fallback adds an optional fallbackMethod parameter that hard-codes 'npm-global', ignoring what detection found. It is near-dead code, since checkouts always have the script and package installs classify as npm.

The package-install branch checks dist/index.js in both check_install_layout and check_runtime_sanity, reporting the same failure twice. Checking for its own scripts in dist/assets is self-referential.
Dropping the scripts/ao-update.sh existence check is an acceptable simplification.
The fallback always uses getUpdateCommand('npm-global'), so pnpm/yarn users are told the wrong command. The 'package-manager update flow' message is generic.
classifyInstallPath no longer requires scripts/ao-update.sh, so any .git at the guessed root counts as a git install, removing a guard against false positives.
The default REPO_ROOT is wrong now that the script sits in assets/scripts. It is only reached on manual runs without AO_REPO_ROOT.
Layout detection by '/node_modules/' substring treats tarball or linked installs outside node_modules as source checkouts, and the runner's value always overrides doctor's own guess.
No written North Star exists; the review measured against the PR description instead. Write one with the user.
Unrequested server persistence changes (save debounce, load dedup, meta persistence, try/catch) unrelated to rotation and absent from the PR description; split out or describe.
Unrequested server change: applyClientUpdate now returns boolean; load/save paths reworked; not in PR description.
Behaviour change: a client update that fails to apply is no longer pushed to the update log or broadcast; undisclosed in the PR.
Type-guard cleanup unrelated to rotation; harmless but unlisted in the description.
safeRotation is exported but not listed among the PR's utilities; stated test count unverified against safeRotation/withRotation coverage.
User-visible result unverified (manual test unchecked); getBounds is not rotated so selection boxes/handles show unrotated bounds, and the PR doesn't state this is left short.
Line hitTest wrapped with withRotation is consistent with renderer; other plugins registering hitTest were not checked or covered.

CSS rotation is applied to the deprecated canvas-engine ShapeLayer; the app uses createDomRendererPlugin whose ShapeWrapper (packages/dom-renderer/src/dom-shape-layer.tsx) never reads rotation, so shapes still render unrotated while hit tests rotate — the rendering claim is false in the running app.
Range includes commit 76f78cbc's server behaviour changes (dropped failed updates, load dedup, debounced saves, meta save) not described in the PR; describe or rebase out.
shapeToBounds now uses the rotated AABB, but getVisibleShapeIds has no caller, so the spatial-index change has no effect and the 'viewport scroll' manual test checks nothing this PR changed.
PR says 22 tests; HEAD has 31 (fix commit added safeRotation/withRotation tests).
safeRotation is exported and used by board-store and shape-layer but omitted from the PR summary.
Frame, freedraw, group, island, connector, counter, board-portal, community-region hitTests are not wrapped with withRotation; rotated instances get rotated AABB indexing but unrotated click tests.

Rotation transform added to deprecated ShapeLayer; live DomShapeLayer has no rotation handling, so hit tests/spatial index treat shapes as rotated while they render unrotated. Apply safeRotation/transform in dom-renderer's dom-shape-layer.tsx.

GPU renderer (active) claims rect/rounded-rect/ellipse/line, and its WGSL never reads rotation (params.w unused), so these draw unrotated while hitTest is now rotation-wrapped; previously both agreed. Implement shader rotation or return null from gpuPrimitive when rotation != 0.
rotation: data.rotation passed raw to the GPU buffer without safeRotation, so NaN/non-number can reach the GPU, undercutting 719aa834's validation.
getRotatedAABB and deltaToLocal are public but their angleDeg === 0 guard lets NaN/Infinity through, producing NaN bounds; sanitize with safeRotation inside.
normalizeAngle(-360) returns -0, normalizeAngle(NaN) returns NaN, snapAngle(x, 0) returns NaN; untested edge cases.
Rotated-AABB path in shapeToBounds has no store test; reverting it would fail nothing.
Marquee selection and frame/group drop target still use unrotated getBounds (also lines 657-667); list as follow-up.
Server changes from 76f78cbc look sound but are undisclosed; corrupt client updates are now dropped rather than saved/rebroadcast — state it or split out.

With WebGPU, the GPU renderer takes rect/rounded-rect/ellipse/line and neither rect nor shape-sdf shader reads rotation (shape-sdf uses params.w for kind); these draw unrotated while hitTest un-rotates the click, and gpu-shape-layer hover is an unrotated box test.

withRotation tests pass with the forgery withRotation = fn => fn: the only rotated case is a 100x100 square at 90°, which maps onto itself. Use a non-square shape at 45° with points inside only after/before un-rotating.

ShapeWrapper and fallback rotate every shape type, but only five plugins wrap hitTest; frame, island, group, freedraw, counter, board-portal, connector and community plugins render rotated yet hit-test unrotated.
collision-utils keeps its own unrotated shapeToBounds, and selection-overlay draws unrotated bounds around rotated shapes.
PR test plan says 22 tests; file has 31; safeRotation missing from the Summary's utility list.
Unrelated server changes from 76f78cbc in range (failed updates dropped, concurrent-load guard, debounced saves); correct on reading but undisclosed.
normalizeAngle(-360) returns -0; no test covers it.

Server persistence changes (load-promise dedup, save debounce, boolean applyClientUpdate, thumbnail type checks) don't serve the rotation request; ~150 lines of review surface, the loaded/loadPromise pattern repeated in two files.
normalizeAngle, snapAngle and deltaToLocal have no non-test caller; could be deferred until a caller exists.
getRotatedAABB already early-returns on angle 0, so caller-side zero checks in shapeToBounds and withRotation are redundant.
Same rotate transform plus transformOrigin is duplicated in ShapeWrapper and the fallback; a small shared helper could simplify it.
